#662 1 2004-08-08T07:52:16Z LittleViking
I spent much of today disecting every part of the Ned-generated level data and I found one feature especially interesting.

The code for the launch pads always looks something like this: 2^414,546,-1,0 . The 2 says that it's a jump pad. The next two numbers are it's x- and y-coordinates. And the final two, the interesting ones, represent x- and y-acceleration. By manually editing the text, then reloading the level, you can change the power of the launch pads.

Positive numbers move the player right and down, negative left and up. Any number higher than 2 or 3 will instantly launch your ninja out of the level.

(Oh and, Mare and Raigan, if I gave away the big new gameplay mechanic of v1.4, I apologize )

#25767 2 2004-08-11T02:17:33Z LittleViking
The number in the corner isn't frames per second. It's milliseconds per frame. So when it says 50, you're getting (1000/50= ) 20 fps. When it's over 100, you get less than 10 fps. Unfortunately, everyone has the same problem. The best you can do is close as many programs in the background as you can (or upgrade your computer).

#25828 23 2004-08-13T02:32:43Z LittleViking
Hey, I found a few new weird glitch things

Giant Ninja - This one's useless, but it's fun for at least a few seconds. Start a blank map and add the code 5^! . It creates a giant ninja, but it's outside the border so you can't play like that (unless somebody finds a way to).

Dead Thwump - Change the heading(the last nubmer) of a thwump(8^) to NaN. The thwump will face down, zap right, and won't chase the ninja.

Alt. Still Bot - You can also change the pathfinding algo(third number) to NaN to keep a bot from moving, but just use the last number like Rahl pointed out; it's easier.

Evil Door - More like glitchy-door-of-annoying-death, but anyways, change the (third number) to -1 on a door(9^) and your ninja will fall into the ground to the left of it and explode.

Confused Oneway Platform - I didn't discover this, but I'll post it for the record. Change the (last number) of a oneway(7^) to NaN. It will look like you can stand on top and jump through the bottom, but instead the bottom is blocked and you fall through the top.

Wheh, I'm done for now.

#26478 49 2004-08-31T06:53:42Z LittleViking
Jump Pad Teleporters

Ok, I finally looked into the idea of using jump pads as makeshift teleporters. And it turns out, that with some trial-and-error, any type of teleporter you want to make is relatively easy to do. See the attached level for some examples.

The first frame after the ninja leaves a jump pad, he doesn't interact with other objects (gold, mines, other jump pads, drones, etc.). You should place a braking jump pad where the ninja is on the second frame after the launch. Or more likely, place the braking pad where you want him to go, then adjust the numbers of the first one.

The ninja will still die if he gets imbedded in a tile, even on the first frame after launch. The giant puff of smoke occurs when the ninja's feet touch ground; I have one example of this in the included level.

EDIT:
Turn off caps lock when you're about to hit a launch pad and watch it frame by frame to get a better idea of how the "teleporting" works.
Attachment (lost): post-10-1093935222.txt

Okay, two methods to find it. First make sure hidden files are showing (My Computer>Tools>Folder Options...>View>Show hidden files and folders. Apply.)

1: Browse to <drive letter>:\Documents and Settings\<user>\Application Data\Macromedia\Flash Player\#SharedObjects\<random letters & numbers>\localhost\n_v13b_userdata.sol

2: Search for *.sol

EDIT: These work in WinXP Pro. I don't know about other OSes. Searching should always work though.

#31873 27 2004-10-13T04:21:09Z LittleViking
I just have to reply here.

Electricity doesn't cease to exist if it can't find a ground. It simply stays at its source in some form of potential energy. If electricity dissapeared without a current, things like batteries couldn't exist.

Also, light never ceases to exist. Ever. Being electromagnetic radiation, light is not affected by friction so it never loses its energy as heat. Light does however diffuse exponentially over distance from its source. This means that it may become too dim to have any meaningful effect, but it's always there.

I'm not an expert regarding rubber, but I know it has very unusual properties. It is considered an insulator, but it is very good at storing static electricity (think, rubbing a balloon in someone's hair. it collects a lot of static electricity). Other insulators (leather could be an example) don't store electricity nearly as well. Rubber in your shoes transfers electricity to the ground, rubber in tires does the same - I don't have a clear-cut answer on the subject; conclude what you will.

...

#32663 4 2004-10-19T05:19:38Z LittleViking
You are just telling him how to save demos and levels from Ned. I think he means the main game save file.

I could never find a way to do it automatically, but you can still copy the file manually. Search for "*.sol" files with hidden files included in the search, and you should find a "n_v13b_userdata.sol".
Copy it to your thumbdrive,
take it to the other computer,
open and close N (to create a save file on the other computer),
search for "*.sol" files again,
and finally, replace the file with the one from your thumbdrive.

Hope that helps.

Competition Entry
Author: Debugged
(0-10) Use of tile set: [3] Most of the map didn't feel fully developed. I especially despised the floor gaurd that flew off the map and the teleporter that fails 2 out of 3 times. The mines, one-way platforms, and the no-snap gold at the bottom all added to the amatuer feel of the map.
(0-10) Creativty: [6] I haven't seen any of this before. Maybe there's a reason for that... (yeah, I didn't take off enough points for the floor gaurd and teleporter above, so you lose points here too)
(0-10) Fun: [5] It was a playable level and was a good amount of fun, if you ignore the low points of the level.
(0-10) Difficutly: [3] Actually, the difficulty was good most of the time, but I couldn't find a way to get past the room with the bounce block surrounded with mines. 4 points off for being impassible...
(0-5) Excitement: [3] I can only ignore the bad elements here for so long.
(0-5) Other: [0] Almost forgot to mention those traps near the end. Not a good idea.
Total: [20]

Ambushed
Author: Igi
(0-10) Use of tile set: [6] The drones really take away from the level, rather than make it better. And again the guass turrets in the top corners can hit you almost anywhere in the level, especially across the top.
(0-10) Creativty: [3] Eh, nothing is really even good here.
(0-10) Fun: [3] Tedious. You die often and there is usually nothing you can do about it.
(0-10) Difficutly: [3] Would be easy if it wasn't for all the dying you can't help. The two extremes are present, but the middle ground is not.
(0-5) Excitement: [1] The missile keeps you moving, but it's just not exciting.
(0-5) Other: [3] Watching the drones start off is fun. Once.

Locked In
Author: 654321
(0-10) Use of tile set: [8] It all worked well. The arrows weren't neccessary - the path is pretty simple - , but you don't lose points fot it.
(0-10) Creativty: [7] Simple designs mostly, but they were new to this contest.
(0-10) Fun: [9] Fun fun. Always a challenge, fast to play, you can hardly ever stop moving.
(0-10) Difficutly: [9] It wasn't an easy map but I could beat it most of the time.

Generator

(0-10) Use of tile set: [4] My biggest issue with this map is the laser drone at the beginning. You either have to sneak out very carefully or wait a long, long time for it to pass. Other than that, there isn't much to this map unless you want to all-gold it.
(0-10) Creativty: [4] Not very creative really. It's just a few simple ideas with gold strewn about.
(0-10) Fun: [5] Eh, better than average I guess but not by much. Very short too.

(0-10) Creativty: [4] Many, many different thump patterns.
(0-10) Fun: [2] There is a bit of fun here but it's completely drowned out by the constant ninja death.
(0-10) Difficutly: [0] Can anyone beat this? This is just too hard.

Weary

(0-10) Creativty: [6] It's a new idea in the contest. Most of the level builds itself once you get the idea to put mines on all of the ceilings and floors.

Zap

#1311 1 2004-11-10T02:29:55Z LittleViking
If you're looking for a challenge, here it is.

You are presented with a webpage, a picture, and text sometimes. Use any means neccessary to get to the next screen. This might include anything from changing the URL or looking at the page source, to searching google for a line from a popular German song. Sometimes you need to use external sound or image editors to find a clue.

You do have to use Internet Explorer, like it says. Some of the screens play important sounds that you won't hear in Firefox, etc. Also, you might stumble onto walkthroughs in your searching; please don't use them, that's cheating.

According to the homepage, only 0.09% of people that begin this riddle reach the final, 30th screen. If you think you're part of that very small group, follow the link and begin.

Begin!

#36378 19 2004-11-14T04:09:03Z LittleViking
Mine started as an inside joke, then became a gaming handle, and now it's an internet profile.

Eating lunch one day at school, one of my friends from the group I was with pulled out a brand-name snack cake thing. The package was labeled "Viking Size!", but we all thought it was too small for any real viking to enjoy. Someone suggested that maybe little vikings ate something that size. I replied that there were no little vikings, the big vikings ate the little vikings. I never really thought it was that funny, but they all thought it was hilarious, so it stuck.

Years later, I had to decide on a name to go by when I played LAN games at my school. After thinking about it for a while I had narrowed it down to a few choices. To make the final choice, I knew people would ask who the new player was and I decided that "Who's Viking?" sounded the best. And thus, I became known as Viking.

Now, obviously, when you try to register a name on the internet you have to assume that common names, such as Viking, are already in use. A name like LittleViking would be more likely to be unused, but to be absolutely sure, adding 001 to the end makes for a completely unique username (by the way, 001 has nothing to do with the year 2001; I hate when people put a year at the end of a username). If you see something along the lines of LittleViking elsewhere, chances are good that it's me.


So there you go.

On a side note, I was inspired by Suki's name anagram to see if there was anything interesting in my own name.
There are probably better anagrams, but this is one I found:
Thar me went, the viking throne.
I never even knew the word 'viking' was in there, let alone the pirate referrence.

This could start a small digital copyright debate I guess.

Some groups are now urging the Supreme Court to look at the betamax decision (that made VCRs legal) and possibly overrule it. These groups see file sharing programs (like Kazaa, Limewire, Bearshare, and others if anyone doesn't know), widely used to infringe music copyrights, growing out of control and think they can stop them by eliminating "fair use" as defined by the decision. Fair use includes such things as making one VHS copy of a movie you bought or making a backup copy of a software CD. In an extreme reading, even listening to a friend's music CD that you yourself didn't pay for could be seen as illegal.


So my question is, what do you think about the whole file-sharing topic?

#37919 17 2004-11-26T01:47:01Z LittleViking
Quote: Arachnid, Nov 25 2004, 05:32 PM
Quote: LittleViking001, Nov 26 2004, 01:24 AM
Could you implement a way to delete a map without losing the votes? I'd hate to lose the ability to delete an awful map just because it's been voted on.
Not easily. An author's average rating is calculated based on the average of the ratings for all hir rated maps currently in the DB. Deleting the map removes it from consideration.
I guess I could simply add a 'deleted' flag, so deleted maps are still factored into calculations. Let me think on it a bit.

In that case, maybe you could just let people delete their low-rated maps. Is it really such a problem if people only leave their best maps?

#42076 40 2004-12-22T01:41:06Z LittleViking
Quote: Rahl, Dec 13 2004, 11:04 PM
Entry #1 for me:
I could understand you missing Rahl's first entry, Maniac. Here it is.


And for the reviews:

Swirly Slide
Author: Tsukatu
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 6/10]: You know what? Some of it isn't symmetrical at all. But the symmetry does play well here.
Uniqueness [ 7/10]: A lot of unique challenges here. The symmetry is nothing special.
Fun [ 8/10]: If you're the kind of person that liked Jump!, you'll enjoy this map. I loved it, but it's definitely not for eveyone.
Difficulty [ 7/10]: F..king insane. Crazy challenge level, and it can get frustrating. But I kept coming back for more.
Excitement [ 4/5]: You're surrounded by death at every moment, waiting for him to let his guard down so you can make your move.
Other [ 3/5]: That part with the mines and the one-ways, just before the floorbot room, I never figured out how to pass that. And since my incompetence is clearly your fault, you lose points.

Total: 35 _ Cult-classic in the making. I only wish it had a better name...


Tiered
Author: Kablizzy
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 7/10]: It is symmetrical and the symmetry plays into the level.
Uniqueness [ 9/10]: Hold up, a survival level? You're just asking for uniqueness points now.
Fun [ 5/10]: Maybe too many guass. It was hard to have fun for long because I was constantly being shot.
Difficulty [ 5/10]: Well, it is a survival map. Those are supposed to be hard. I just wish there were one or two less turrets.
Excitement [ 5/5]: Of course it's exciting. Who wants to play a boring survival level?
Other [ 2/5]: There were a few places that were safe to mostly just do nothing at. Specifically, the bottom corners.

Total: 33 _ Can you handle the Evil Bunny's challenge?!


Defangantar-Ixmelerion
Author: Eli
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 6/10]: It's very simple, but it is perfectly symmetrical. On both axes too.
Uniqueness [ 6/10]: Like I said, it's simple. No gold? What were you thinking?
Fun [ 7/10]: About average in the fun department. You really had to think a litle bit to win.
Difficulty [ 7/10]: It's tough if you're impatient. If you can wait for the drones to pass to a safe distance, the challenge drops.
Excitement [ 2/5]: The missile-dodging could be exciting sometimes.
Other [ 2/5]: Not much left to say. I wish there were gold and/or mines here.

Total: 30 _ A simple map that's still very good. But I like my gold.


Differences
Author: Rahl
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 9/10]: The symmerty looks good and plays very differently in each part.
Uniqueness [ 8/10]: It is unique. What more can I say?
Fun [ 5/10]: Here's the problem with this level. I just didn't have a lot of fun playing it. A lot of parts were slow and there was some random ninja death by the guasses.
Difficulty [ 4/10]: Very easy if you ignore the gold. Much, much more difficult if you try to get all of it.
Excitement [ 2/5]: I've gotta say, I found most of it tedious. Some parts near the guass were intense, but still not really exciting somehow.
Other [ 3/5]: Nothing left to say, so you get a 3 here.

Total: 31 _ Great example of how to do symmetry well, but not the best as a level.


Deified
Author: Kablizzy
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 9/10]: It looked cool, it played into the level, and it was perfect.
Uniqueness [ 9/10]: The tileset is as unique as it gets. The playable area is good too; it's different
Fun [ 9/10]: The only way to play is to get everything. If you don't go for everything, it's just not as much fun.
Difficulty [ 9/10]: It was easy, but you couldn't let your guard down. Full completion runs are so much fun on this level.
Excitement [ 5/5]: No question. Between the gauss dashing and avoiding the seeker drones, it's just amazing.
Other [ 3/5]: Sometimes, maneuvering around your tile formations can be difficult. Specifically, getting from the middle to the top.

Total: 44 _ Fast, fun level. Go for everything.


Was it a cat I saw?
Author: Gohan
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 10/10]: Tons of objects, all symmetrical. The top parts play just as well as the bottom, but very differently.
Uniqueness [ 10/10]: Unique like crazy. Awesome job making something different.
Fun [ 6/10]: It's never amazingly fun, but it gets the job done. Unfortunately, little missteps that end in ninja death occur far too often.
Difficulty [ 4/10]: It's long. A little too long. And most of the dieing happens because you got stuck on a tile and gaussed for it.
Excitement [ 4/5]: You came close to death over and over in this map. However, there are some dull places and downtime.
Other [ 4/5]: Nothing bad left to say really.

Total: 38 _ It seems a newcomer is reaching for the NedCon crown.


Dance of Death
Author: Makron
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 6/10]: Eh. It's symmetrical. It works. Nothing special.
Uniqueness [ 5/10]: None of it was all that unique, really.
Fun [ 7/10]: Playing felt like a chore, but at least it was one of the fun chores. Like checking the back yard for pirate gold.
Difficulty [ 8/10]: Not a cake walk, not a snuff film. It was somewhere inbetween; like a cake film, or a snuff walk.
Excitement [ 5/5]: Sure was exciting. Never a boring moment.
Other [ 2/5]: Small complaint: At the end, when you go to jump up the right wall to the exit, there's a one-way there to stop you. I know it keeps the symmetry, but it was annoying the first few times through.

Total: 33 _ A perfect example of an average map.


Road Rage
Author: Maximo
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 10/10]: Of course it's symmetrical, Maximo made it. Each part plays so differently from its counterpart that it doesn't even feel symmetrical. (That's a good thing.)
Uniqueness [ 9/10]: It's unique too. I've never seen anything quite like this.
Fun [ 9/10]: It was lots of fun and never got frustrating.
Difficulty [ 8/10]: It's fairly easy but always challenging. If you go for speed, then it's hard.
Excitement [ 4/5]: It was always exciting, but there could be times when you had to wait for a thwump to pass.
Other [ 4/5]: I lost my mind trying to make a super-fast demo on this map. Somehow, this will affect your score.

Total: 44 _ An excellent map from one of the masters.


Bomb Diffusion
Author: Makron
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 3/10]: It's great symmetry, but that's not all this category is about. It's also about how it plays. And I never got to play the majority of it. So: (9 for symmetry + 1 for how it plays)/2 - 2 for the "LV factor" = 3 points
Uniqueness [ 8/10]: Very unique indeed. For a reason...
Fun [ 2/10]: Some trial-and-error to get started. Then death.
Difficulty [ 0/10]: I couldn't find the way to beat it. Impossible map gets a 0.
Excitement [ 3/5]: It's definitely exciting, but I can't play most of the map. That makes me angry.
Other [ 0/5]: It looks like you put a lot of thought into this map, but playing it tells a different story.

Total: 16 _ Where do you go once you reach the wall?


Generator2
Author: Lartsa
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 7/10]: The objects weren't perfectly symmetrical. It plays well, but there's nothing really special about it.
Uniqueness [ 8/10]: I'd say a lot of the challenges here are unique.
Fun [ 9/10]: It's a challenge, and it's always exciting. This makes it a lot of fun to play.
Difficulty [ 8/10]: It's almost perfect for a challenging map. You only lost points for the homing launchers (which I despised), and I thought it was a bit too long.
Excitement [ 5/5]: Alsolutely exciting. Throughout the map. You always had the feeling that you could escape whatever danger you were in.
Other [ 2/5]: I really feel like I should take away a couple more points for the rockets. Man, I hated those...

Total: 39 _ Another quality map from Lartsa.


Shards
Author: Eli
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 6/10]: Yep, that's symmetry. Plain and simple.
Uniqueness [ 6/10]: I wouldn't call it unique, but it is new and different. ...What? Oh, I just defined unique? Fine, whatever.
Fun [ 6/10]: It's fun once you gain some momentum, but you sure do die a lot.
Difficulty [ 2/10]: Did some judge traumatize you as a child?! Is that why you hate us?! Too hard.
Excitement [ 2/5]: The excitement is generally short-lived, as death looms it's lonely reaper ever o'er our young ninja's brow.
Other [ 3/5]: I can't decide if I like the lasers or not, so they get an average score.

Total: 25 _ It's just too hard. What more can I say?


O45
Author: rrrobyp
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 5/10]: A lot of the objects aren't symmetrical. And the symmetry plays pretty well into the level. Not great though.
Uniqueness [ 9/10]: Ah, the category that's indepentent of everything else about the level. This is very unique. I don't know if I've ever seen anything like this.
Fun [ 3/10]: I could never get the timing right to pass the drones. That isn't fun.
Difficulty [ 2/10]: Same problem getting past the drones. It was hard to repeat, and you were expected to repeat it several times here.
Excitement [ 1/5]: Let's see, there's the beginning where you do some mine jumping, then the middle where you die. Neither of those parts were exciting.
Other [ 3/5]: Besides that outer ring of drones, the level wasn't bad.

Total: 23 _ Nobody likes drones in a small diagonal tunnel.


Rescue Agent N
Author: Igi/Ande
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 6/10]: The symmetry wasn't quite perfect, and it didn't play well in several parts. It was still pretty intricate so you get points for that.
Uniqueness [ 8/10]: It was unique too. I like how the mine parts played completely differenly on the top and bottom. The one-way platforms also added to this category.
Fun [ 5/10]: The difficulty issues kept it from ever being very fun. See Below.
Difficulty [ 2/10]: This was hard. A few too many enemies, the one-ways really just got in the way, and there was just enough random death to be annoying.
Excitement [ 4/5]: Yep, definitely exciting. There were a lot of close calls if you're good enough. Of course, there was also a lot of dieing...
Other [ 1/5]: You're not losing points for this, but I don't see why it had to be a rescue mission. I don't see why any map has to be a rescue mission.

Total: 26 _ Homing rockets and seeker drones in a room full of semi-random one-way platforms. Bad combination.


Mirror, Or Rim?
Author: Rahl
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 9/10]: It looks good and it plays well. Obviously, the two identical halves still play very differently.
Uniqueness [ 9/10]: I've never seen anything quite like this. It's all new.
Fun [ 8/10]: I enjoyed it. You have tons of choice in how you play it.
Difficulty [ 8/10]: It's hard until you find a path you like. Then it's still challenging, but not "hard" really.
Excitement [ 3/5]: Not the most exciting, but there was always some excitement.
Other [ 4/5]: It all looked great except for the doors covering the exits. I wish you could have made that look better.

Total: 41 _ Player's choice! You make the level!

#46266 189 2005-01-15T22:15:52Z LittleViking
Lofty
Author: Maximo
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 6/10]: Eh, it's pretty simple symmetry, but it plays into the level.
Uniqueness [ 10/10]: Gotta say, I've never seen a level like this. Nothing like this at all.
Fun [ 5/10]: It's a challenge. I don't know if I'd call it a fun challenge. But it can be pretty fun at times.
Difficulty [ 4/10]: It's hard to pull off even when you know what you're doing. And you aren't given any direction. You really have to figure it all out on your own.
Excitement [ 5/5]: Couldn't be more exciting. You're in constant danger and the danger only multiplies when you try to progress higher.
Other [ 3/5]: The appearance makes it look like a n00b map. The thwump walls just aren't something I'd expect to see from Maximo.

Total: 33 _ Very unique concept. A must-play, if only for that.


Rooms 7
Author: Lartsa
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 3/10]: The tiles are symmetrical. Very simple symmetry, and it doesn't really affect the level at all.
Uniqueness [ 2/10]: Rooms 7. You've done it six times before. Nothing special about the symmetry either.
Fun [ 4/10]: Too long. Too easy to die. Tedious most of the time.
Difficulty [ 3/10]: Generally it's easy, but you can die at any moment. The long-ish load time gets annoying fast.
Excitement [ 1/5]: Not really exciting at all. It was mostly easy and tedious until you got killed unexpectedly and had to start over.
Other [ 2/5]: The tileset is almost entirely made using the solid tile. That really took away some of the level's potential.

Total: 15 _ Nothing about this level really makes it worth playing.


Circle of Death
Author: tktktk
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 9/10]: The symmetry's good and interesting, and it defines the way you play the level.
Uniqueness [ 8/10]: Very unique play style. I haven't seen anything like it before.
Fun [ 7/10]: Fun enough up until the end. Reaching the exit switch and the exit were too hard to be any fun.
Difficulty [ 6/10]: A pretty good challenge, until the end. It got frustrating playing the whole level so many times just to die again at the end.
Excitement [ 3/5]: Once you get used to playing, getting the switches isn't really threatening any more.
Other [ 2/5]: That mine below the exit switch was evil. I forgot about that almost every time I dropped through.

Total: 35 _ Fun and unique, but the end is too hard.


(Already judged "Rahl - Differences.")


A War at Tarawa
Author: JeR(K)
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 6/10]: It gets the job done. Nothing special.
Uniqueness [ 6/10]: A lot of variety, but nothing is really new here.
Fun [ 7/10]: Pretty fun at times. There's a list of complaints in the Other category that disrupted the fun a bit.
Difficulty [ 7/10]: You could die at any time (and you do die a lot), but the level was still beatable.
Excitement [ 4/5]: More exciting than some levels, less exciting than others.
Other [ 0/5]: Moving around on the tiles was awkward is several places. The one-way/door area at the top was also hard to get into. Most of the time, I just fell through to the exit switch because of a glitch. Getting up the sides on the top was hard sometimes with the guass there. Also, I always expected to do one side of the top then the other; I skipped past the middle and got killed more than a few times.

Total: 30 _ Plenty of variety, but also plenty of minor problems.


Tentacles
Author: Igi/Ande
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 10/10]: Plays very differently on the symmetrical parts, and it looks good.
Uniqueness [ 8/10]: I've never seen anything exactly like this.
Fun [ 8/10]: Fun to play too. There's tons of room to go for speed.
Difficulty [ 8/10]: It's a challenge. Never too hard, never very frustrating.
Excitement [ 5/5]: Very exciting, what more can I say.
Other [ 3/5]: Nothing good left, nothing bad.

Total: 42 _ Fun, good-looking map. Definitely worth playing.


insert plaindrome here
Author: Brickman
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 4/10]: The top and bottom played differently, but the bottom felt kinda broken.
Uniqueness [ 6/10]: The top third of the level is especially unique, the rest just isn't really.
Fun [ 4/10]: Never much fun. The top is mindless, the bottom is tedious, and the middle is frustrating.
Difficulty [ 2/10]: Very easy until the end, which I found difficult. I've never really liked drone puzzles like that.
Excitement [ 1/5]: You have to keep moving the whole time, but you're only in real danger at the drones when you're moving slowly and carefully.
Other [ 3/5]: Nothing about this map makes it deserve a rating below 20.

Total: 20 _ An interesting, but forgettable, map.


Dammit, I'm Mad!
Author: Brickman
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 10/10]: Great! They're the same, but the play so differently. And both parts are awesome fun.
Uniqueness [ 8/10]: Mine-jumping isn't new, but the launch pad thing is as far as I know.
Fun [ 9/10]: Once you get used to playing, it's actually a very fun level. Going through it smoothly is just saucy. And I don't use that word "saucy" lightly.
Difficulty [ 9/10]: Getting yourself killed is pretty hard, but winning is no walk in the park either. The challenge level is about perfect, but it can also get frustrating.
Excitement [ 5/5]: The tension never lets up.
Other [ 4/5]: Your concept of pissing the player off instead of killing them was refreshing.

Total: 45 _ A Jump! style map with a twist.


Lonely Tylenol
Author: Ainigma8
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 4/10]: It looks cool but it plays like crap. And the symmetry never really makes a difference here.
Uniqueness [ 2/10]: The tile arrangement is new, but the low quality is a popular thing on Numa.
Fun [ 0/10]: I didn't have any fun at all playing this. None at all. Just too frustrating.
Difficulty [ 1/10]: I'm not going to beat that.
Excitement [ 2/5]: It's intense, but it's also quite frustrating.
Other [ 3/5]: Wait... Are those chickens? You get points for chickens.

Total: 12 _ A sexy map with no personality...


Closer and harder
Author: rrrobyp
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 5/10]: The symmetry here doesn't serve the level is a big way, but it works.
Uniqueness [ 8/10]: No, you don't get a reason.
Fun [ 7/10]: Pretty fun most of the time, but there was a lot of random ninja death, especially at the top when you're trying to get the exit switch.
Difficulty [ 6/10]: The random death made it harder. Frustration set in after a while.
Excitement [ 5/5]: Very fast-paced excitement. Reminds me of 5 laps in a way.
Other [ 0/5]: Random ninja death.

Total: 31 _ Too much random death to be a great map.


Think, stupid, think!
Author: tktktk
--------------------------------------------------------
Symmetry [ 4/10]: The symmetry doesn't add much to the level, except making you do everything twice.
Uniqueness [ 10/10]: Everything here is new. All of it.
Fun [ 8/10]: The beginning started to get tedious, and the rest of it was really challenging.
Difficulty [ 3/10]: It was just too hard. I never beat it in one go. Great challenge, but it would have been more rewarding to finish it.
Excitement [ 5/5]: Intense the whole time.
Other [ 4/5]: I spent way too long trying to beat this.

Total: 34 _ Very challenging level with a bit of Cubish Syndrome.

Of course, the first thing you think while trying to disprove (not disapprove ) this theory is reason that you have a choice to do action A or action B. I could say "flim flam" right now but instead I'll say "doo dee doo." Now you have free will. But then you start thinking that you were destined to say "doo dee doo" in the first place and, again, you don't actually have free will. After that you'll go back to thinking you can act for yourself (the happier idea to live with); it's a pretty circular argument but at least it's a fun one.

Now don't get me wrong. I'm exactly the type that would normally cling to a concept like this. I, however, stand by the idea that I have choice, completely unaffected by physics and chemistry. I've put too much thought into this to be convinced otherwise.

#49940 18 2005-02-10T05:29:38Z LittleViking
I keep switching back and forth between "your locked-room analogy is off-base" and "your locked-room analogy is perfect." On the one hand, it fits in a metaphorical way; the room representing your actions (as well as all other events of all time throughtout the universe) that you're locked into even if you think you are making your own choice. On the other, most people won't see any metaphor; I am physically in the room I'm in now and I choose not to leave. The door isn't locked. Is that pre-destined? Depends on what you believe.

When I said that free-will was the happier idea to live with, I was referring to the general population, not specifically myself. I do that a lot. Free-will, I think, is one of those things like religion that people are just happier believing in.

I don't believe that there is randomness in the movement of subatomic particles. I believe that everything can be quantified, calculated, and predicted. While this becomes more difficult as you move from a very small scale (say, a dozen atoms) to a complicated system (like an apple falling from a tree), it would still be possible given the capacity to calculate such a system. Yet still, I don't think that removes my ability to choose freely.

I think that, as a human machine, I gather input and act accordingly, unconciously firing the required synapses and stimulating the necessary cells to bring my actions to the world. I'm sitting here, resting my chin on my fist, thinking about how to word my thoughts, not because of some inevitable chain of atomic collisions but because it's what I chose to do at this moment. There was a time I believed in what I now know is called determinism, but after thinking about it, I choose not to.

Quote: "PC Gamer"
Quote: "Floorplans of death"
N is the physics-powered, minimalist Flash platform game in which a ten-pixel-tall ninja, N, jumps and flips around while evading murderous drones. It comes with Ned, the level-editor, and there's a huge community of hardcore N players (well, more hardcore) producing amazing new levels all the time.
Levels range from the quite literally imppossible Survival maps to the Newtonian spectable of 'DDA's. It stands for Don't Do Anything, and levels of this kind are Machiavellian Rube Goldberd devices of near-death, shoving and catapulting your ninja into deadly traps from which he is rescued at the last split-second by a Deus Ex Machina platform or jump-pad.
N itself is completely free and on the discs, along with these five brilliant levels and the next five best. Thousands more are to be had at numa.notdot.net.
Quote: "IT'S MY NIGHTMARE"
Every good DDA features some close shaves, but this one virtually skins N's chin. Author Sendy openly teases you by flinging N into situations you realise are fatal at the exact moment you're saved from them, riding an emotional rollercoaster at breakneck speeds.
Quote: "LIGHT FANTASTIC"
The Light Fantastic is a more stylised DDA. N is dropped into an arena dotted with no fewer than nine laser drones, and is shoved around by the friendly end of 'thwumps' while beautiful patterns of laser light converge angrily wherever he was a thirtieth of a second ago.
Quote: "MISSILE RACE"
Race levels are essentially regular levels with superior flow, meaning you can work up enormous velocity as you hurtle round them, bouncing off walls and using the game's physics to accelerate. As an added incentive, this one also has a swarm of homing missiles chasing you.
Quote: "CHALLENGE #9"
A series of ultra-simplistic levels by N-expert TKTKTK, the Simple Challenges are more like tutorials than conventional levels. Each of them seems utterly impossible at first, but once you grasp the principle he's trying to teach, they're merely very difficult. Think fast.
Quote: MOUNT DOOM
Hard beyond words, but one of the most satisfying levels. The red mines that make up the 'lava' are so dense and devilishly placed only the nimblest of ninjas will find a path through to the top. Once inside, you've got a Gatling Drone and Thwumping stalactites to face.

#52608 6 2005-03-05T01:57:00Z LittleViking
Good:
- Gold. Must be some gold.
- Mines. At least a few.
- Flow. Gotta make it quick and exciting, good flow will make even the easiest levels fun to play again.
-Room for players to improve. If you know you can make a faster demo, then you might keep playing. If you have no reason to replay it, then you won't.
- Large scale. I've seen very few people get this right. MetaNet got it, and their levels are superb. I don't know how to explain how to make a god scale but generaly just avoid tiny clutter, keep the entire play area in mind.

Bad:
- DDAs, Rescue Missions, and (to a lesser extent) Boss Maps. Just personal turn-offs maybe, but they annoy me enough to make the list.
- Hidden enemies. Especially laser drones, gauss turrets, chaingun drones, and thwumps.
- NaNs Seeing a gold piece at the top border is just so unprofessional.
- Trial and error. Any form of it. If I have to die before I know the exact path I'm meant to take, I'm unhappy.
- BACKTRACKING TO THE EXIT WHICH WAS AT THE BEGINNING OF THE LEVEL. Ahem, sorry 'bout that. After a long winding level, never force the player to go back through it to the beginning. When I get an exit switch, look for the door, and see it waaaay back at the beginning, I stop playing and don't come back to it.
- Near-impossible endings. After I've gotten all the switches and I'm ready for the final bit of challenge before the exit, I don't want to have to run past a drone with perfect timing or perform a pixel perfect jump between mines or make a mad dash before the newly-released horde of chaingun drones spots me.
- Door glitches. When I come across a door glitch, I know the final level wasn't tested. That's annoying.

There you go. That'll do for now.

Now introducing, official N chat.
Method of choice is IRC.
Now, before you get scared and leave, we've made it as easy as possible for everyone to join in the fun.

Quote: Kablizzy
Ah, the wonders of IRC. IRC? What's that you say? Internet Relay Chat is one of the oldest forms of chat and most addicting on the net. If you already know about it, then don't let me stop you! If not, then let me introduce it to you! IRC is an excellent way of opening new doors in growing communities, just like ours. mIRC and Chatzilla are perhaps the most popluar IRC clients available.

Server: irc.waypasteleven.com
Channel: #n

General rules for the IRC channel can be found here.

Rules for #N:
1) Be respectful. Blatant insults and/or picking fights will not be tolerated.
2) This ties in with Rule 1, but go easy on the language. A censored cuss word every once in awhile is not going to kill anyone, but there is no need to continually use cuss words to get your point across.
3) Spamming is frowned upon in the channel. This means flame wars, posting nonsensical things over and over again, et cetera. You guys are bright, you know what spamming is.
4) Have fun!

Note: If kicks for bad behavior persist, banning from the channel altogether is an option.

Feel free to use it 24/7.

If you already have an irc client, you can join up with us by going here in your web browser: irc://irc.waypasteleven.com/N

You can also use the forum redirect link at the bottom of the general forum category.

If you don't have an IRC client and want to come in and talk, there are a few ways to join in on the fun! First is mIRC, one of the most popular clients around. It can be found here:

http://www.mirc.com/get.html

There's also have a web client, for those of you who don't wish to download an IRC program or can't because of a school firewall, which can be found here.

If you have troubles reaching the #N channel, try reading the next post. If that doesn't solve your problems, post about it here or PM LittleViking001 or I. We'll make sure you can get in.

No longer will you have to sit in the active users tray waiting for some forum activity (you all know what I mean).
#61497 2 2005-04-23T07:25:07Z LittleViking
If you're having trouble joining, read this post.

Quote: Kablizzy
If it's your first time using IRC here's how to connect with mIRC:

Quote
Download mIRC and install it. Open the program and the Options window by File > Options (OR just options, if you're with the shareware version)... . There you can configure your server list (numa.notdot.net) and your personal information such as your nickname for chat. When you're finished, click "Connect to IRC Server" and wait for the server to log you in. From there, to access the channel you type in...

/join #N

... and you're there! That simple. If you have any questions, feel free to ask and I will try and help. I am also new to IRC and only know what I have managed to figure out. I've figured out mostly how to boot people. It's basically all we ever do.

For those who are having trouble getting into IRC:

Download mIRC
Open it
Click File OR Tools, depending on your version
Click Options
Click ADD (to add new network)
Type in the Description: Numa
Type in the Server: irc.waypasteleven.com
Type in the Port (s): 6667
Click OK
Click Connect to IRC Server

Once you do that, you will get a white screen that will say connecting to numa.notdot.net. There will be a "chat bar" at the bottom. Type in there:
/join #N

That should bring you into our channel.

And here's how to connect with Chatzilla:

Quote
Download Chatzilla
From your Firefox browser, go to Tools > Chatzilla
When Chatzilla opens, go to Tools > Options
Under Global settings, click the startup tab
Scroll down to "Auto-connect URLs"
Click "Add"
In the popup, type in "irc://irc.waypasteleven.com"
Close Chatzilla, return to your Firefox browser, go to Tools > Chatzilla, and you're there!

#64035 229 2005-05-07T01:45:26Z LittleViking
Just quick reviews. Had a free moment and took advantage. If you want a more detailed review of your map, request it and I'll get to it another time.



Map: Tombs of Giza
Author: so_what?/nevermore

The missile part is rather frustrating. The beginning is too easy; you're just going through the same motions over and over getting to the missile part. The thwump/gauss area was nicely done. Really, this map is all about the missile area. I found it too hard, and not in a challenging way, more in a nothing-you-can-do-but-die way.

27/50


Map: Arrow'd!
Author: so_what?/nevermore

Not much in the style of MetaNet. Actually, it's not really MetaNet style at all. The difficulty is well balanced; there is some trial-and-error, but it's not bad. One complaint I have is that the chaingun drone is completely pointless. No reason at all to have that there. At first glance, the arrow style is kinda cool; it's not implemented as well as it could have been though.

24/50


Map: Viscosity
Author: tktktk

Woo! Quite a challenge. Doesn't look bad. It can be a bit frustrating at times. You have to be fast and stay precise, the core of N's gameplay.

40/50


Map: Phrenology
Author: so_what?/nevermore

Rather long, I thought.

32/50

#65648 4 2005-05-14T07:20:17Z LittleViking
We don't have hover-vehicles because of the cost-benefit ratio. Hovering 4-6 ft. off the ground offers almost no benefit over a traditional ground-based vehicle.

The problem, of course, is making it work. Your idea is huge thrusters. Tanks are rather heavy; the thrusters would have to be extremely powerful, wasting tons of power and fuel that could go to better causes, like traveling longer distances.

You also have to think about the recoil from a tank turret; there's a reason helicopter's don't fire tank shells (they would lose control and crash, if you don't know).

Ground-based battlecruisers are completely unneccessary. The whole point of boats is simulating land, on the water. We have artillery guns for land; we have guided missiles; we have infantry. Floating battlecruisers serve no purpose.

Also, hovertanks wouldn't be able to easily take down large ships. Ships are made to not sink; they take a lot before they'll go down. And either way, warships have stronger guns with more ammunition than a tank would anyway.

So there you go. Hovercraft just aren't practical. Name something a hovercraft could do well, and I'll tell you that there's something that already exists that'll do it better for less money.

July 26. I make my first submission to Numa. A short, easy map, but it looked good. A nice preview of what my style would be one day.
July 28. I join the forum. A step into the community that will hold me here indefinitely.
July 30. I beat N v1.3c and Maximo's 'Mount Doom' in the same day.
August 3. I submit 'Artificial Intelligence' to Numa. What I consider my first really good map.
August 7. Thread 771. Manual Nediting.
August 30. Teleporters are disected and explained in the manual nediting thread.
September 9. The teleporter tutorial. (Wow, that's been downloaded 224 times as of this post.)
November 3. Woot. I'm a moderator.

#3385 1 2005-06-20T05:03:44Z LittleViking
[Quote equals Kablizzy.]

Well, kids, here we are.

There are some things on my mind that I'd like to get off my chest here. First off, the attitudes around here. These need to stop. Now. I, and the other staff members, have been more than lenient with all of you on this stuff, and the flaming, whining, and bitching about menial things has gone way too far. We aren't here to baby-sit you guys; we're here to have fun, just like everyone. And when that fun degenerates into what it has, it's no longer fun.

I understand that you guys are young, and not as mature as I probably expect yall to be, since, after my initial experience here with all of you, I had some pretty high expectations of you all. But with the attitudes that have been shown around the forums lately, I can see that those expectations were indeed far too high. When I signed up as a mod here, I did it because this was an awesome place to be, the community was nurturing and welcoming, and things were going well. But the flaming and conspiracy theories and spamming have ruined that thoroughly, as has the influx of new people to Numa, and the aftermath.

Which brings me to my next point. Yes, we were planning another fiasco. LV and I have had it in the works for months now, and with NC7 so close to opening, it was the prime chance to step things up. But that, too, has been thoroughly ruined, due to the sour and bitter attitudes of some of our forum members. With that said, I feel you all deserve an explanation here, to clarify what exactly these fiascos meant to our community.

When the Kablizzy fiasco went off, it wasnt to confuse and anger you. It wasnt meant to create a rift in the forum, nor was it intended to frustrate you all. And it went off without a hitch. Everyone had fun, everyone had a laugh, all was groovy. And then came the Y&BB. The Y&BB was intended to be fun and interesting; something for yall to participate in, enthrall yourselves in, and have fun with. But most of you whined and moaned that we were conspiring against you all, and that we were abusing our moderator powers in order to conspire against all you little people. Where that came from, and what purpose it served, I still have no idea, but I didnt appreciate the sentiment then, and I certainly dont appreciate it now.

We had a discussion back in January, I believe, about forum activity waning. And it was decided that the Y&BB was an excellent chance to get you guys more involved in the forums, and it did so. The Y&BB was a smashing success. Beyond the handful of bumps in the road that our more scurrilous members provided to it, the entire Y&BB went over quite well, and ended more famously than I had hoped it to end. When forum activity waned a while back, we had another discussion, and it was decided to implement an IRC channel, which seemed to revitalize interest in the forums, as well.

So, back to the new fiasco we were planning. We had Arachnid set up a fake Numa for us, which can be found here. We dubbed this map archive Supernuma. We were going to put Supernuma everywhere, and come up with fake news, a fake about system, all that good stuff. We had gone through many versions of this prank before this particular idea fell into our laps. Weve been considering an elites lounge for quite a while now, but we hadnt actually thought about implementing it until about a week ago, or so. So, shortly afterwards, you guys happened to come up with the very same idea, which fit quite nicely into our plan. So, our idea was to make NC7 be maps exclusively from Supernuma, the elite lounge of maps, thus creating a bit of an uproar on the forums as to why certain people werent invited into this elite club, thus creating the backdrop for the prank. However, with all the discussion recently over actually implementing such a system, our goals rather fell apart for the prank actually succeeding, as a particular member has decided for us.

So, part two of this was going to be, eventually, to give people access to the only actual page on Supernuma. Within that page, well, well get into that in a minute.

So, my next beef here. As most of you know, Im suspended until the 24th. And now, for whatever reason, Polymatic and Kablukatu have been dealt with in a similar fashion. Which is the very reason why this isnt being posted on one of my own accounts. This wouldnt bother me as much if it werent in conjunction with all the other stuff that has gone on, which Ill go into shortly.

Now, going back to the maturity thing here, I believe that we, as a community, began as incredibly mature, and massively fruitful. But I have seen that maturity go to hell over the past months. And I do have a beef with Keron here. Throughout my time here, Keron has overtly asserted his maturity level as greater than the remainder of us, and, for the most part, he has lived up to that assertion. However, I feel as though he has been quite overprotective of the staff positions here on the forums. I feel as though, even in our most dire times, he has refused to provide the forums with a working administrative staff, particularly when we most needed it, even though he wasnt going to be there to fill the position himself. There were many, many times when simply adding one of us to temporary Administrative staff would have alleviated much heartache and much trouble for all of us, but due to Kerons severe unwillingness to do so (Whose motives for refusing to promote any of us are still unknown to me, beyond speculation), our forums suffered for it. Even the decision to promote one of the mods to a global moderator was an excruciating task on his part, when it was obvious to the remainder of the staff that it was the bare minimum that was required for the boards to remain functional, and much more action, such as one of the mods gaining temporary Admin status, was ideal. So, now, the time has come when Keron is out of school. Thus, since my Global Mod position was a temporary one, so I could watch over the forums while he wasn't available as admin, we apparently don't need a Global Moderator anymore. And Im sure all of this will sound pretty self-righteous and pretentious, but I assure you, this is a view shared by the entire moderator staff. Not only have LV and I proven ourselves more than worthy to take care of the forums, but were Maximo around, he would be in the exact same position, as well. By that same token, when we were lacking an Admin, Kerons only answer was to take his chances instead of appointing a temporary Admin in his stead. Which, in the eyes of the moderating staff, is a horrible judgment call. Particularly after my appointments around my other forums to Administrator and Moderator, Keron still hesitated. Im not sure what harm it could do to have an extra Global Moderator around, nor do I understand what kind of complex Keron must have to make him believe that he needs to keep his Admin position sacred from us filthy mods, in spite of what good it may have done for the forum. Overall, I think Kerons lack of maturity overcomes his better judgment at times, and cant see the benefits that certain actions would hold due to this seeming lack of common sense. This isnt meant as an Attack on Keron, as he has done a wonderful job on the boards, and has done many, many things to make these boards a wonderful place, but to inwardly assume that we arent worthy of Administrative duties and abilities - based, I assume, upon a fear that one of us would turn malicious - is unwarranted, and I feel that it has hurt the forums as a whole.

So, between all of this, Ive butted heads with a lot of you. And from that, Im sure Ive been seen as an elitist bastard, and of that, at least, I am guilty. But between the .sol sharing from trib4l, Brickmans flaming, the debates, the spamming, and all of the crap that goes on here just to push my buttons and see how far things can be pushed, it has broken my spirit. The last thing I want to do when I come home at night is to babysit and make sure that no ones flinging poo at each other. So, armed with this, we all made the decision to go ahead with our final prank.

So, back to that page I was referencing on Supernuma. Once the users got access to that page on Supernuma, it would hold my resignation from Metanet staff. With the stresses of my Staff positions on the sims, as well as the ridiculous crap that has been allowed to go on here - only some of which Ive covered - as well as the plethora of real-world issues that need to be dealt with, Its best for me just to step down from Metanet Staff before Keron goes through with my demotion. I feel as though Keron wishes to keep the moderators to the absolute bare minimum amount of functionality required to keep the boards running, and no more. This, on top of the suspension of all three of my accounts, on top of TDLs saucy little outburst(s) over something that was meant to be fun for you guys, on top of the remainder of the forum hijinks, was more than enough to make my decision.

In addition, for the good of the community, particularly after this, Ill be leaving the community on a more-or-less permanent basis. Being here as much as I have been has proven to be quite detrimental to my life, and my relationship with my fiance, my job, and my future in school have all suffered heavily due to the amount of dedication Ive put into staff here, and I think its time to concentrate more upon my family than upon this, when it has become so unfulfilling. It was a good run, and I can revel in being such a large part of the Metanet community for so long, and I will always carry the memories that weve all created. For the vast majority of the time that I was here, I enjoyed my time here immensely, getting to know all of you on a more personal level than I have been allowed to know almost anyone. For the past year or so, you all have been my family, the people whom I come home to every day, the people I associate with on a daily basis, and those who have been closer to me than my own family has been.

So, a couple final thoughts. First off, Im going to be relinquishing the NTTS site to Daddaluma. If he, or anyone for that matter, wishes to take it up, ask Daddaluma to talk to me, he has contact with me over at HoI, and I will send him the html files needed to reconstruct the site elsewhere.

Secondly, TTK, I havent forgotten about you. I cannot get into my PMs right now, due to my suspensions, but just as soon as I can, Ill be resolving things with you, as well.

Thirdly, and perhaps most importantly, the Kablizzy Fiasco, NTTS, Nedcons, and the Y&BB were, without a doubt, the pinnacles of my time here, and they will not be soon forgotten. Speaking of which, get to judging NC6 so we can move on to the actual NC7, the theme of which, I will announce here. The theme for Nedcon 7 will be Maximo-style maps, to herald Maximos return. I hope that provides for some extra reason to finish judging.

With all that said, it is time to say farewell. If ever you wish to chat, or just to say hi, you all know where I can be reached. Goodbye, Metanet. And good luck to you all.

***Marked***

I know it's been suggested before. People seemed to like it but it would be too hard to implement on a database system like Numa has now. I think the ratings system would be more accurate if people had more incentive to rate maps that fall past the first page or two.

So, I suddenly thought of an easy way to have random maps. Rather than 10 random maps on a page, the link could give you maps in their current order, with only a random start point. The link would basically look like--> numa.notdot.net/browse?start=<random number here>

And the great thing about this idea, is that it could be implemented independent of Numa. If Arachnid doesn't find it neccessary, it could just as easily be put on N-vision, or any simple javascript ..script. I don't know how it took so long to come up with this idea, but it's here now.

Pseudo-Edit: Hm. Seems the rating system is going away. Well, still, there's nothing wrong with playing a random set of maps from the past.

#78841 10 2005-06-27T10:03:14Z LittleViking
I'm starting to feel like I'm the only one who doesn't built at least most of the tileset first. I start with whatever part of the map I want the ninja to begin at, build a chunk of the level, mess with the tiles to get some style, and move on to the next part. When it's all finished I smooth it out, work out the flow, ease up on the difficulty, and generally polish it up.

EDIT: I forgot to mention the most important parts of my map building. One: being different. You'll see it in everything I do, from the placement of a thwump to the tiles I choose. Little bits of my levels are as unique as I can make them, if only to give the player an experience they're not used to. Second (and less important), is filling out a level. You don't want parts of your level to be empty, but you also don't want it to become too long and hard. Fill in empty space with simple challenges that reward the player with gold.

Find a map you like on Numa. Click in the Map Data box. Press Ctrl+A to Select All. Ctrl+C to Copy. Go into N. Press ~ to go into debug mode. Click in the top box (labeled "level data"). Okay. Here's what I got. Help me if you're interested (though it looks like it's just Maniac and me at this point...).

Riddle #1. death.
Edit the image so the stretched text is readable and you'll see that text and a series of numbers at the bottom. Numbers are in the format <#,#,#> <#,#,#>... Now I'm guessing that means look at the stretched text at <line, word, letter>. Working that out almost gives a real word: deoth.
Edit: The third set of numbers in this image is 2,4,3. If it were 2,5,3, the word actually would be death. I'm gonna call this a mistake on Meteor's part and go with death.

Riddle #2. open.
We are give several quotes from various parts of the forum. All seemingly unrelated. However, all of them have a few words in common. "The," "and," and "open." Now, I think "the" and "and" are too common to be the password here, so I'm going with "open."

Riddle #3. 236,792,586.
Soduko puzzle. I had never heard of soduko before, so I searched google. Lucky me, the very first result was a soduko solver. The clue also tells us that the answer is in numbers. No need to try translating to letters.

#95045 157 2005-08-29T09:11:25Z LittleViking
Well I gotta say I had fun. Um. Thanks for keeping it going even though I was the only really active participant. Thanks to nevermore for the dusty password, even if it was wrong. And... I don't know, lots of thanks to TDL for starting this.

I... I... I...

Excuse me, I'm kind of speechless. Heh, good thing I wasn't speechless earlier. Twelve words, eh? Twelve words...

So the world is saved. So... the world isn't going to end. What do we do now? Go back to life? That'll take time. All the death and destruction isn't going to go away with twelve words. Think about it, people, this is no small event. This is no flashflood on the six o'clock news. This is no geo-political conflict, remembered for years to come. This is more. Religions could form around those twelve words.

And yet I can't help but think I did more harm than good with what I said. Can humanity really return to what it was? ...Does it want to? Maybe we can build it better. Or maybe we'll fail. Whatever. Last thing on my mind right now. I leave that to the rest of the world; I can't control everyone, no use trying. ... Not tonight anyway.

No, tonight I return to civilization in a different way. I've done my job, and everyone else can get back to life when they choose. But when I look out at the world now, the first thing I see is darkness. For the first time in what feels like forever, the brightest light in the sky is the moon. I'm sick of people complaining about these. We need to discuss and define them, and probably should have a long time ago.

Double-posting. Double-posting occurs when you make a post, then make another post two minutes later when you should have edited instead. Perfectly understandlable that someone who's new to forums would miss the edit button. If you see this happen, simply tell them to edit their post next time. Now, most of the time, when I see someone apologizing for a double-post, they're not doing what I would consider a double-post. If you were the last person to post in your personal maps thread and you post again several days later, it's not a double-post. If you were the last person to post in a very old discussion, and now you have something new to add, you're not double-posting. Even if you just want to bring attention to a thread that hasn't been touched in a few days, you're not double-posting. Like I said earlier, a double-post occurs right after the initial post; when you should have edited instead of posting again.

Thread resurrections. Why do you people hate these so much? It's not like it does any harm. Also, there's no such thing as a ten-day resurrection. Or a five-day resurrection, or a two-week resurrection. A resurrection is a couple of months or more. Falsely calling out a necromancer is no better than spam, especially considering how many posts I see like this that add nothing to the conversation.

I had been conscious before anyone else in the room "this time." That was always my style. Lie there, pretend to still be asleep. Gather information. It was hard not to get up when the one boy was attacked. But now is the time to get into things.

"Bud? I go by LV."

The doors are scary. The doors mean death. I don't want to die. So what else is there? The midget.

"Can you tell me anything about this midget and his shack? It's the only logical start point I can think of. He doesn't seem interested in anything but staying in his shack. Why is he so protective of that? Was he always like this?"

And suddenly I'm struck with a wave of distrust.

"... And what is it about you that makes you think we should trust you. As far as any of us know, you're part of this horrible place. You could be lying about the clock... your clock. I don't know what I'm expecting; convince me you're worth trusting."

He's right, the slopes of the lines are different. The red triangle has a 3/8 slope (0.375) and the green one has 2/5 (0.4). Obviously, the total area of the shapes doesn't change.

The difference in slopes cuts a small triangle off of the top one, and adds a small triangle onto the bottom one. The difference should come to about one square in area, and thus make up for the square that was removed.

#103780 382 2005-09-26T07:39:35Z LittleViking
Warning: Some swearing below. Don't go complaining about it.

LittleViking (LV)
===

What now? I was speechless. Everything we had, it pointed to that door. All the clues were in order, all the work we had done up to that point... and now it was all for nothing. We were wrong somewhere or we were wrong everywhere, there's no way to tell. Another short pause in thinking before I can manage to speak again.

"... Fuck."

We're out of leads now. All we can do now is sit here forever, or pick a door and die. And it's all the god-damned clock's fault. I turn to the clock and tell it how I feel.

"What the hell do we do now, clock? What are we supposed to do? We've done everything, we've been careful. We found your damn clues and we know what they mean. What more are we supposed to do!"

By this point, I'm walking toward the clock with a mad glint in my eye. I'm not thinking clearly enough to tell you if it's mad-anger or mad-crazy, but from looking at me, you'd probably think both.

"What have you ever, ever, done to help us along? You wait around and kill our friends, and what do you ever do to help! Not just our friends either; you kill our enemies, you kill our acquantainces, you kill everyone. For what? What do these people do to deserve becoming a fucking pile of ashes! Just because we enter your room, your god-forsaken room?"

"You wanna show us the way? Point me in the right direction, timekeep, right now. You've done nothing but tick away since we got here and I can't take it anywmore, so if you got anything else to say, now's the fucking time."

I'm still worked up, but everything that needs to be said had been said. I'm a step from the clock and staring at it. Waiting. Waiting for an answer. It's the clock's turn to reply.

#103882 391 2005-09-26T20:02:52Z LittleViking
LittleViking (LV)
===

I didn't want to hear what Archie had to say. He was telling us we were wrong, and I don't want to be wrong. People die when we're wrong.

I ponder on the numbers for a while.

"Caesar's death by the month divided. Caesar died on the fifteenth of that month, or near it. Fifteen by three divided is five. Maybe it was doors divisible by five we had to eliminate."

Adding the east and west walls back in, taking out the even and prime numbers, numbers divisible by five, and running a BAD/OK test on what was left, I had a new set of numbers.

"9, 21, 27, 39, 57, 63, 77, 81, 91, 93, 99. Eleven doors. 'When the days equal the doors, look to the clock, for all is done.' 'When all else is done, the clock provides the direction and the key...' I think we're really ready to move on now."

I look to the clock and wait for a reply, just like before. This time though, the glint in my eye is hope.

#4729 1 2005-10-12T18:46:31Z LittleViking
I was assigned to write an evaluation essay recently in English class, and I decided to do it about N. I just got the paper back today, and it got a 100% grade so I decided it was worth posting here.

Quote
The computer video game, N, is the first release from Metanet software. Available for free download at the developer's website (www.harveycartel.org/metanet), the game is easily accessible to anyone interested. The style of N is minimalistic, using light gray against dark gray to fill most of the screen. The game only uses three controls: left, right, and jump. Levels in the game are meant to be beaten quickly too. Each set of five levels has a 90 second timer, and that's usually more than enough time to finish them. Yet despite its simple appearance, N can be much more enjoyable and offer more hours of play than any of today's best-selling titles.
In N, you control a small ninja jumping and running around each level. You can't attack your enemies here though. You're only allowed to avoid them, but this part of the gameplay doesn't take away from the fun. It actually adds to it very much. A total of 500 levels make up the game, which easily provides over 100 hours of play. Every five levels should take a total of under 90 seconds, but you're expected to die and repeat each level many times before completing it. Inspired by games like Lode Runner, you are presented with a whole game board at once and can try to plan how to solve it without getting killed. In this way, it has some elements of a puzzle-type game. N always keeps players thinking, planning ahead, and learning from their mistakes.
The part of N that makes it stand out on top of all other 2D platformer games is the perfection of movement. Perfectly fluid player control keeps people coming back. Watching the ninja move, it really feels like it knows what it's doing. Animation is fluid, dynamic, and realistic. The precision of control allows players to improve their technique endlessly. The game's best players will easily spend hundreds, or even thousands, of hours playing levels to perfection. Also present to keep the game fun is the ragdoll engine that activates after death. The ninja will flop onto the floor, or break into pieces and be flung around the level. Since death is such a common occurrence, it's nice to have something fun to watch between plays, plus it helps stave off frustration.
There is a way for those people to show off the skills they develop. Online highscore tracking is built into the game. The 20 fastest times for every level are viewable in-game or on the developer's website. Even after finishing all 500 levels included, people will often go back to them over and over to get onto the top 20 list. (Teacher's Comment: Obsessive compulsive people?) Players here can get highly competitive, playing the same level for hours at a time in hope of cutting a tenth-of-a-second off their time. Despite how fast players get however, others can always find ways to improve highscores. Since the movement in the game is so precise, holding a key for an extra 1/40th of a second can mean the difference between first place and second.
More casual community can be found in the map-making element of the game. Every copy of N has the N-Editor, Ned, built-in. This tool gives every player the same capability to make levels that the developers had. People can use the tools given to create and test levels they make themselves. Once a person is satisfied with their creation, the level can then be saved into a small file and transferred to others to play. The online N User Map Archive (numa.notdot.net) houses over ten-thousand different user-created levels, which can easily be imported into the game using Ned.
For even more interaction with other players, players can visit the game's forum (metanet.forumer.com). Players can chat casually about the game, complain about it, ask for help, or talk any other subject unrelated to N that comes up for discussion. People are encouraged to bring attention to especially good maps at the Map Archive. Competitions are constantly running to challenge the best map-makers' creativity. Each competition has a theme, such as building symmetrical maps or only using a specific few objects.
Like every game, though, N has its problems. One is the technology required to play. Even though its appearance is simple, it tends to run slowly on older computers. Gameplay can become choppy and make it difficult to perform the precise movements required to play. This is a problem because the difficulty of the included levels also increases very quickly. Relatively few people ever finish even 100 levels, let alone all 500.
Despite its few drawbacks, all of the different features of N add infinitely to the amount of time you can spend playing the game. N is a game that every gamer should take a chance to play. On top of everything else, it's offered for free on the internet. The community is friendly and at the same time competitive. If that's still not enough to convince you, N has the one key element that every game hopes to achieve: it's fun.

#4812 1 2005-10-20T09:18:23Z LittleViking
This thread is meant to be a discussion for a future thread. Similar to the Map Rating Thread, people would post maps and other people would run demos for those maps. The thing I noticed about the map rating thread is that, even though a rating is posted for each map, little feedback is included. Most maps on Numa don't get demos for them, even if the map is painfully easy for the veterans that visit here.

So my idea is a thread with rules for people to post maps and get demos for them. Here are my ideas for the rules (probably what most of the discussion here will be about):
1. Every map gets a demo.
2. Only three maps can be up at one time. The small number should help avoid confusion and losing maps in the thread.
3. To avoid death of the thread if three impossible-to-beat maps are up, there will be a time limit before they're eliminated. After one week with no demo, a map is taken off the list of three. (This takes precedence over rule one, obviously.)
4. Anyone can post maps. This won't be like the rating thread where you'd have to demo a map before you could post one. I'm sure the new players want demos for their maps too.

I was also thinking there should be a system that gives frequent demoers priority in the list of three over new posters. People who contribute a lot to the thread should be rewarded. The problem is, I don't know what kind of system would be good for this, or what would ever work. You tell me.

So, if people like this idea, let's finalize the details and make the thread official. Gimme your opinions.

#4874 1 2005-10-25T03:32:35Z LittleViking
The idea is simple: Post a map and someone will create a demo for it.
Here are the rules.

1. Every map gets a demo.
2. Only three maps can be up at one time. The small number should help avoid confusion and losing maps in the thread.
3. To avoid death of the thread if three impossible-to-beat maps are up, there will be a time limit before they're eliminated. After one week with no demo, a map is taken off the list of three. (This takes precedence over rule one, obviously.)
4. Anyone can post maps. This won't be like the rating thread where you'd have to demo a map before you could post one. I'm sure the new players want demos for their maps too.
5. Only one map per author can be on the list at a time.

Ideally, people will post maps that don't have any demos on them already, but you can also post a map with a specific goal attached.
For the people who do the demos, you can leave comments about the map here if choose. It would definitely be appreciated.

Edit: Added rule 5.
Edit: Just to be safe, and since I didn't mention it before, demoing a map implies a completion demo. You can't just make a quick demo with the ninja dying to get a map off the list.

#118965 41 2005-11-29T04:35:07Z LittleViking
Quote: brickman, Nov 28 2005, 03:26 PM
Which snap are we using? 1/2? 1/4? Obviously not no snap. Also, does two different object types on the same spot count as stacking?

No-snap is really 1/24 snap, which is what we're using. (23*34)*(31*24) = 410,688 possible positions for objects. And as for the stacking, I'd consider two different objects on the same stop to be stacking. I'll make exceptions from stacking doors though, including the exit door. The switch counts as the position of it, and the door can be anywhere.

Now, and I didn't think about it before, the exit door has the most variation. Since I'll allowing stacking (because the switch represents the object, not the door), that means for every position the switch could be in, there are 410,688 variations (one for each possible position of the door).

So, even if this is the only object in the game, there would be 410,688^410,688 different combinations. This is even higher than the 10,000^500,000 rough estimate that got me that other number.

Cathy has six pairs of black gloves and six pairs of brown gloves in her drawer. In complete darkness, how many gloves must she take from the drawer in order to be sure to get a pair that match? Think carefully!!
Assuming there are right- and left-hand gloves, 13. She could take six left-hand black and six right-hand brown and still not have a matching pair, but the next glove would have to give her a complete pair.

Quote: MetaNinja, Dec 30 2005, 01:18 PM
flip a penny and a dime and hide the result from you. "at least one of the coins came up heads", i announce. what is the chance that both coins came up heads?
The possible outcomes if one is guaranteed to be heads are: penny is heads, dime is tails; penny is tails, dime is heads; both are heads. And out of three possibilities, one is correct, so the odds are 1/3.

I've gotta say, I'm ashamed of all of you. Sure, he could have looked around here and read the files that came with the game, but that doesn't mean you can't offer some help when he asks for it.

Now for zaka, there are two ways you can play levels (which you'll find at http://numa.notdot.net ). There's debug mode (in Ned) and userlevels mode.
To play in debug mode, start up N and press ~ to go into debug mode. Copy the "Map Data" from Numa (not the "1.4+ Map Data") and paste it in the top box. Click outside the box and press L to load the level, then press P to being playing. To play at normal speed, turn caps lock on.
To play in Userlevels mode, you need to enter the data into your userlevels.txt file. For that, simply open the userlevels.txt, scroll to the bottom, and paste the "1.4+ Map Data" from Numa. For the Userlevels mode to work, you need to have the N executable and the userlevels.txt file in the same folder.

Hope that helps.

@Keron: Do you think science teachers don't believe evolution? Of course they do. Whether evolution occurs really isn't even debated in the scientific community because evolution is a long-accepted fact of the natural world. You see it in biology, yes, but also cosmology, geology, chemistry, sociology and psychology if you count ideological evolution. In a broader sense, evolution is part of the base of every science.

Keron, your arguement about the world being perfect for life is often ridiculed as a "lack of imagination arguement." To honestly believe that life couldn't have formed under any other conditions than those seen on Earth is unimaginable. Life on Earth has formed in the most extreme climates, from the depths of the ocean to the ice caps to volcanic spouts and swamplands and irradiated grounds and salt lakes, and so on and so on.

About teaching creationism is school, I've always gone by Lucidium's way of thinking. People are already taught about God in church, so why should we force it on the students with different beliefs?

@Keron: By sermon disclaimer, he meant the same type of disclaimer you're asking for for textbooks. At the end of each sermon, the preacher would have to say, "Now, some people believe that the universe was not formed by God, but instead formed by natural means. This may explain the fact that there is no observable or repeatable evidence in all of history that would prove that there is a God."

Pseudo-edit: Also, you use the term "theory" as basically a way of saying that it's probably false. When scientists say something is a theory, it means there is no question in their mind that it is correct. Scientists can spend their entire careers developing a theory, and to say that it's unreliable just because of the "theory" marker is like discrediting their entire life's work all at once.
